name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Platform and task adaptation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the person’s primary task and the target platform before translating a screen. Read that platform’s procedure; use Principles to resolve hierarchy and Designing for games only for gameplay.
2. Compare navigation, window/scene model, primary input, attention duration and state restoration. Preserve the product task while changing the interaction appropriate to the destination platform.
3. For device changes such as opening an iPhone Duo or resizing an iPad window, specify what selection, editing state and route survive each transition.
4. Deliver a platform-decision matrix or an adaptation patch, with concrete acceptance scenarios for each materially different interaction.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

# Apple HIG: Task scope, interruption and dismissal

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify whether the task needs inline content, a temporary presentation, an independent window or a scrolling container. Use Modality before choosing a blocking surface when interruption is in question.
2. Enter the specific Alerts, Sheets, Popovers, Panels, Windows or Action sheets procedure to resolve anchoring, size, urgency and platform-specific behavior.
3. Name every meaningful exit: commit, cancel, back, outside click, gesture, close or interruption. Preserve unfinished work and restore the parent selection/focus where appropriate.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ios
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPhone experience for handheld touch, interrupted use, orientation changes, and system entrypoints.
---

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ipados
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPad experience for resizable multitasking, a larger canvas, mixed input, or prolonged creative work.
---

# Use the iPad canvas without assuming exclusive space

Read [Designing for iPadOS](../../references/designing-for-ipados.md). Inspect the task, related content, current navigation, window assumptions, and supported touch/Pencil/keyboard/pointer paths. Identify whether people hold the iPad or work at a stand/table. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode and revise only the authorized surface using the existing stack.

Decide which relationships benefit from simultaneous visibility. Keep a list beside detail or tools beside a canvas when that reduces navigation; leave unrelated information out. Replace repeated full-screen transitions or modal panels with persistent contextual structure when space permits. At compact multitasking widths, collapse that structure while retaining selection, draft, and the route back to context.

Map each meaningful operation to the inputs the task supports. Touch remains usable without attached accessories. Precise pointer selection and keyboard commands can accelerate work; Pencil may create or annotate content without becoming a required substitute for ordinary controls. Let input methods change during the same task without discarding state or hiding essential commands behind hover.

For cross-app work, specify what can be dragged out/in and where imported content lands. Treat resizing, orientation, larger text, and another app's presence as normal operating conditions. If the iPad experience runs on Mac, identify the Mac adaptation work rather than claiming identical behavior is already native.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a sheet-music editor copies its phone flow: choose score, open full-screen tools, then return to the page after each change. Decision: editing needs score and tools together, but multitasking may narrow the window. After, a contextual tool column accompanies the score at regular width and becomes a dismissible panel at compact width, preserving page, selection, and undo history. Touch editing and keyboard commands reach the same operations.

Deliver a wide/narrow task flow and input mapping or corresponding implementation. Fail if shrinking loses a selected object, a pointer-only control blocks touch, or imported content silently replaces work. Use supplied evidence for findings; physical reach, Pencil response, and inter-app drag/drop remain unverified until exercised on supported devices.

Continue with [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for resizing, [Apple Pencil and Scribble](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-apple-pencil-and-scribble/SKILL.md) for drawing/writing, or [Pointing devices](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-pointing-devices/SKILL.md) for precision input.

name: apple-hig-popovers
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting temporary anchored information, choices, and their dismissal or save behavior.
---

# Anchor temporary work without losing it

Read [the popover guide](../../references/popovers.md). This workflow is application advice; do not assume dismissal semantics from visual style.

Inspect trigger/source, related task, selection count, edits, platform/width, and create/review/adapt request. Identify essential reference content that must stay visible and every available dismissal route. Distinguish transient help/choices from persistent tools and warnings.

Anchor the arrow closely to its source while preserving context. Keep dimensions fitted to content and one popover at a time; replace the old one rather than cascade. Multi-selection stays open until explicitly dismissed. For automatic nonmodal dismissal save work; discard only through explicit Cancel. Add Done/Close/Cancel only when they clarify completion/saving. Use an alert for warnings that cannot be accidentally missed. On compact iOS/iPadOS layouts adapt to a sheet/fullscreen presentation; tvOS/watchOS do not support the component. On Mac detachability may suit persistent reference work, with continuity into panel form.

Implement the anchor/selection/dismissal behavior or supply a transition/size specification; reviews must identify the exact accidental-loss or context defect. If only screenshots exist, label outside-tap saving and replacement behavior as checks rather than observed failures.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a tag popover closes after the first choice and discards edits when a second toolbar button opens another popover. Decision: multi-selection and automatic dismissal need retention. After: keep it open for multiple tags, retain committed work on automatic dismissal, and close/replace it in one activation with explicit Cancel for discard.

Deliver the artifact and anchor, size, selection, save/cancel, and adaptation contract. Verify outside dismissal, explicit Cancel, multiple selection, replacement, and narrow width. Fail for lost work, warning-only popovers, cascades, or obscured essential source context. Report native positioning/animation/accessibility execution separately.

Load [sheets](../apple-hig-sheets/SKILL.md) for compact adaptation, [panels](../apple-hig-panels/SKILL.md) for persistent Mac tools, or [alerts](../apple-hig-alerts/SKILL.md) for critical warnings.

---
name: apple-hig-sheets
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting a short parent-related task, sheet sizing, step navigation, and dismissal protection.
---

# Keep the sheet scoped to its parent task

Read [the sheet guide](../../references/sheets.md). This procedure is application advice; sheet modality and placement differ by platform.

Inspect the parent/task, steps, unfinished edits, window widths, platform, and create/review/adapt mode. Determine whether the task is short and related, ongoing supplementary work, or a complex editor. Record Done/Cancel/Back/gesture outcomes separately; one screenshot cannot establish data protection.

Choose another workspace for substantial editing or repeated input-and-observe work. Keep one main-interface sheet at a time. Define Cancel/Close as exit without saving, Done as finish/save, and Back as step navigation; avoid all three together. For iOS/iPadOS choose useful detents with a grabber for resizing, protect edits on vertical dismissal, and use standard centered iPad sizing. A composition flow may need large-only rather than medium-only confinement. Nonmodal sheets can support supplementary iOS/iPadOS work. Mac sheets block their parent while allowing other windows; repeated adjustments fit panels. VisionOS sheets center in the field of view with parent context visible. Watch sheets are brief occasional custom tasks, never content navigation, with unmistakable leading dismissal.

Implement the task/exit/size behavior, create a step-and-exit contract, or review specific loss/navigation defects. Preserve the user's stack and verify capability before naming an API implementation.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a phone message composer is medium-only, stacks an attachment sheet, and labels its first-step exit Back. Decision: composition needs room and one understandable task route. After: use a suitable large composer, internal attachment navigation, Cancel/Done on the first step, and Back only for returning within the task; dismissal resolves unsaved work.

Deliver the artifact, step actions, detents, parent availability, and data outcomes. Verify clean/edited gesture dismissal, Back, completion, resize, and replacement. Fail for lost drafts, modal stacking, inaccessible completion, or Back that exits. State native gesture/grabber/assistive checks separately.

Load [modality](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-modality/SKILL.md), [action-sheets](../apple-hig-action-sheets/SKILL.md), [panels](../apple-hig-panels/SKILL.md), or [windows](../apple-hig-windows/SKILL.md) according to task length and exit needs.

# Designing for iOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. An iPhone experience must work both during brief checks on the move and through extended games, browsing, or media sessions. People switch among apps frequently. ## Best practices - Design for a medium-sized, dense display viewed at roughly 1–2 feet, usually held in one or both hands. Accommodate portrait and landscape use. - Keep primary content and actions clear, with secondary operations reachable through a small number of interactions rather than many simultaneous controls. - Support touch gestures, onscreen keyboards, and voice; use motion sensors, nearby spatial interactions, or personal information only where they improve the task. - Put frequent touch controls within comfortable reach, commonly the middle or lower display. Preserve swipe-back navigation and list-row gestures. - Adapt to orientation, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type without breaking context. - With permission, use platform data and services to reduce typing: location, biometric authentication, and payments are examples. - Integrate appropriate system entry points: widgets, Home Screen quick actions, Spotlight search, Shortcuts, and activity views. Their familiar behavior helps people act outside the main app. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

# Designing for iPadOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ipados) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. iPad supports portable entertainment, detailed work, and creative activity. Its large high-resolution display may be held, placed on a table, or used on a stand; typical viewing distance stays within about 3 feet. ## Best practices - Elevate useful content with the larger canvas. Reduce modal interruptions and full-screen transitions; keep controls reachable without obscuring the work. - Choose content density and sizing for both viewing distance and current input method. - Support combinations of touch, onscreen keyboard, attached keyboard, mouse or trackpad, Apple Pencil, and voice. Mixed-input workflows are normal. - Expect both quick actions and hours-long sessions. Support several visible apps, multitasking, and inter-app drag and drop rather than assuming exclusive use of the display. - Adapt continuously to orientation, multitasking sizes, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type. Preserve a coherent experience when the iPad app runs on macOS. - Consider widgets, multitasking support, and drag and drop as integrated parts of the experience. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ipados) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

# Popovers Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A popover transiently exposes a small related set of information or tasks above content after a control or interactive region is activated. ## Best practices Use it for temporary functionality instead of a persistent space-consuming panel or sidebar. Point its arrow closely at its source while keeping that source and essential reference content visible. Supply Close, Done, or Cancel only when the choice clarifies confirmation or saving; ordinary dismissal can happen outside the bounds or after a choice. Keep multi-selection popovers open until explicitly dismissed. Automatic nonmodal dismissal must save work; discard changes only through explicit Cancel. Show one popover at a time without cascading another from it. Close the current one before opening a replacement, ideally in a single activation. Only an alert may appear above a popover. Keep dimensions limited to the content, and animate size changes to preserve the impression of one continuing view. Describe tasks rather than using popover terminology in help. Use an alert for warnings because popovers are easy to miss or dismiss accidentally. ## Platform considerations No additional visionOS rules are specified. Popovers are unsupported in tvOS and watchOS. ### iOS, iPadOS Reserve popovers for wide layouts. Adapt compact layouts to use the available screen with a modal sheet or other suitable full-screen presentation. ### macOS Consider detachable popovers when people may need to keep information visible while doing other work. Dragging can turn the popover into a panel; change its appearance minimally so the relationship remains clear. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) [Action sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/action-sheets) [Alerts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts) [Modality](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit

# Sheets Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A sheet supports a short, scoped task closely connected to its parent, such as choosing a save location or attaching a file. ## Anatomy Sheets are modal on macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. iOS and iPadOS also allow nonmodal sheets that affect the parent while leaving it interactive. Cancel/Close dismisses without saving; Done finishes or saves; Back moves to an earlier step rather than dismissing the sheet. ## Best practices For lengthy or complex tasks, evaluate fullscreen editing/media presentation, a separate Mac window, or a visionOS Full Space. Keep only one sheet from the main interface at a time. Close an existing sheet before a new one, restoring it later if necessary. For ongoing supplementary work, use nonmodal iOS/iPadOS sheets, macOS panels, or a visionOS split view. Pair Done with Cancel or Back to make an alternative route clear, but avoid showing Cancel, Back, and Done together. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS For a single-view sheet, Cancel belongs at the leading top edge and Done at the trailing edge. In a multistep flow, the first step can show Cancel with disabled Done, subsequent steps Back with disabled Done, and the final step Back with enabled Done. Resizable sheets rest at detents. Large is fully expanded; medium is about half height; custom heights are possible. Large is automatic, adding medium permits both, and medium alone prevents full-height expansion. On iPhone, medium can reveal common content first while allowing expansion; composition flows often benefit from large only. Show a grabber for resizable sheets: dragging changes height, tapping cycles detents, and VoiceOver can use it. Support vertical swipe dismissal and use an action sheet to resolve unsaved changes. On iPad, prefer centered page/form styles with standard sizing over a dimmed background. ### macOS A rounded card floats over and dims its parent, but other app windows remain usable. Choose a useful default size, with resize support where expanding helps. Bring forward the parent and its modeless document panels on presentation, and allow other windows to come forward before dismissal. Repeated input-and-observe workflows belong in a panel rather than a sheet. ### visionOS The sheet floats before its dimmed parent. Center it in the field of view instead of emerging from the window bottom. Keep enough parent visible for context, and consider optional resizing. ### watchOS A sheet slides over the screen with semitransparency and system blur/desaturation. Use it only for a brief occasional task requiring custom title or content; alerts and action sheets better fit basic information or choices. Do not use sheets as content navigation. Keep the leading dismissal unmistakable; if replacing its default label, use a suitable SF Symbol rather than Back or a page-like title. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Modality](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/modality) [Action sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/action-sheets) [Popovers](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers) [Panels](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/panels) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: March 24, 2026, March 29, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023, June 5, 2023.

description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting layout hierarchy, safe areas, size classes, resizable windows, enlarged text, or platform-specific spacing.

# Preserve relationships while available space changes

Read [Layout](../../references/layout.md). Inspect content priority, navigation, controls, supported environments, constraints, and current implementation. Identify design/review/adaptation mode and keep the existing layout system. Record actual available space and text/localization conditions; device names alone are insufficient evidence for a breakpoint.

Start with relationships: align peers, group related items, indent subordinates, and reveal secondary choices progressively. Place important content toward the leading/top region in the locale's reading order. Separate backgrounds that can extend beneath bars from important content/actions that must respect safe regions.

Choose adaptations from available width/height and environmental values, not a phone/tablet or portrait/landscape guess. Preserve selection, content, functionality, and idiom when columns collapse, actions overflow, or horizontal rows stack for larger text. Test the smallest and largest useful layouts first, then intermediate resizing, longer localization, direction changes, and display accommodations. Crop decorative backgrounds without distorting aspect ratio or hiding essential imagery.

Apply platform conditions deliberately: Mac essential controls cannot depend on a bottom edge that may be offscreen; TV content needs the guide's overscan insets and focus-expansion room; Watch normally needs very few side-by-side actions. visionOS windows/volumes should resize, use meaningful bounds, and avoid inline 3D crowding controls; use separate volumes for model-centric work. Read numeric platform specifications from the guide rather than generalizing one platform's spacing.

**Before → decision → after:** A reading list positions Delete at a fixed bottom coordinate and fixes each row to one line. Decision: resized windows and enlarged titles need flow-based layout. After, row height/wrapping adapt, secondary actions remain reachable through contextual overflow, and the selected article persists when the sidebar collapses.

Deliver corrected layouts/constraints or implementation plus an environment matrix. Fail if a required action disappears, related items detach, content overlaps hardware/bars, or resizing changes the task's meaning. Report tested dimensions/settings; static or Linux checks cannot establish native safe-area/focus behavior absent supported execution.

Use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md) for text behavior, [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for direction, and [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md) for 3D position/scale.

This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Use predictable relationships among content and controls while adapting to the actual available space. ## Visual hierarchy Prioritize important content toward the top and leading edge in reading order. Use system components for RTL adaptation. Align related items, indent subordinate items, and group relationships with space, containers, or separators. Reveal secondary choices progressively through disclosure, menus, nested views, or scrollable media sections. Distinguish navigation/controls with Liquid Glass and scroll-edge treatments; extend full-window backgrounds under bars and sidebars. A background extension effect can mirror and blur imagery under adjacent components instead of hiding essential original art. ## Adaptability Handle size classes, display sizes, orientation/aspect ratio, Dynamic Island, external displays, Display Zoom, resizable windows, text changes, localized length/direction/fonts, and date/number formats. Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout, safe areas, margins, and layout modifiers. Orientation-locked games must still resize. With large text, stack horizontal content, increase row height, and allow wrapping. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can supply Dynamic Type in games. Preview smallest/largest layouts first, then multiple devices, localizations, sizes, iPad resizing, and iPhone Mirroring. Scale backgrounds to fill without distorting aspect ratio; extreme wide/short or narrow/tall windows may crop much more than standard displays. ### Size classes Each axis is compact or regular, describing available width or height rather than device type or orientation. All four combinations can occur as apps resize, multitask, or mirror. Base layout on these environmental values, not idiom/orientation guesses. Preserve functionality across classes while changing how much is exposed, such as sidebar versus tabs or visible actions versus overflow. The platform idiom remains the same during resizing, so preserve its familiar character. ## Guides and safe areas Layout guides supply rectangular regions for alignment, spacing, margins, and readable text widths; custom guides can add app-specific structure. Safe areas exclude edge obstructions such as camera hardware, status bars, tab bars, and toolbars. Keep important content and controls within the appropriate safe regions. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS rules are listed. ### macOS Do not rely on the bottom of a window for essential controls because it may sit below the physical display. Avoid placing content behind the top camera housing. ### tvOS Inset primary content 60 pt vertically and 80 pt horizontally to withstand TV overscan/settings. Leave enough focus padding for system enlargement so focused items do not obscure important information. #### Grids Use consistent row/column spacing, sufficient room for enlargement, and symmetrical partial items at both horizontal edges. Add extra separation above and below row titles. UIKit collection flow layout derives the column count from item width and spacing. Source grid measurements follow; all use 40 pt horizontal gaps and a minimum 100 pt vertical gap between unfocused rows. #### Two-column grid Unfocused item width: 860 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Three-column grid Unfocused item width: 560 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Four-column grid Unfocused item width: 410 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Five-column grid Unfocused item width: 320 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Six-column grid Unfocused item width: 260 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Seven-column grid Unfocused item width: 217 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Eight-column grid Unfocused item width: 184 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Nine-column grid Unfocused item width: 160 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. ### visionOS Support resizing in windows and volumes; center content horizontally at very large sizes. Set minimum/maximum bounds only to avoid overlaps or unwieldy layouts, not to disable resizing. Use inline 3D content sparingly for meaningful additions; inset it so it avoids controls and window edges. Prefer volumes or immersive spaces for large/model-centric content. # Transient formatting palette — revised specification

Platforms: iPadOS and iOS. The palette edits formatting for the current document selection. It remains a short contextual task; it is not a persistent inspector. No framework or deployment version is specified.

## Presentation and layout

- A Format control opens the palette and captures the selected content as its editing target. Keep that target stable while using palette controls.
- In a regular-width environment with sufficient space, present one content-sized popover. Anchor its arrow directly to the visible Format control's bounds, updating the anchor as the window changes. Keep the control and essential selected-content reference visible; never point into empty space.
- Show primary formatting choices together. Reveal secondary formatting options inside the same surface with disclosure and an internal detail view. Back returns to the primary choices without saving, discarding, or closing. Never cascade a second popover. Animate content-size changes as one continuing surface.
- In compact width, use a modal sheet occupying the available width instead of tiny floating geometry. Start expanded at the large detent, with a scrollable body and fixed, reachable completion controls. Use standard centered sheet sizing on iPad when this fallback is needed. Do not offer a medium detent in this initial specification; therefore no resize grabber is needed.
- Select the surface from the current size class and usable space, not the device name. If a regular-width popover cannot fit its content while retaining the anchor and essential reference, use the sheet fallback. Keep controls inside safe areas; wrap/stack content rather than shrinking it. Short heights and enlarged text must retain access to every choice and completion action through scrolling.
- Resize or rotation transfers the active session between surfaces without a second presentation, commit, rollback, or reset. Preserve target, selected choices, draft, internal route, and scroll position where applicable. If the source control becomes unavailable, use the sheet rather than retain a detached arrow.

## Editing and exits

Maintain an opening baseline, a working formatting draft, and a stable target. Choices update a preview of that draft on the target; a preview is not yet a document commit. Each choice stays selected visibly. Both single and multiple choices leave the palette open so people can make a sequence of adjustments.

| Event | Required outcome |
|---|---|
| Done | Commit the draft to the target, dismiss, and return focus to Format. |
| Cancel | Explicitly discard this session's draft, restore the baseline preview, dismiss, and return focus to Format. Previously committed changes remain intact. |
| Tap outside wide popover | Commit the draft before dismissing. Never discard work. The dismissing tap must not also edit underlying document content. |
| Activate another contextual popover trigger | Commit and close the current popover, then open the replacement in the same activation. At most one popover is visible. |
| Back within detail options | Return within the same palette; retain all draft choices. |
| Tap outside compact modal sheet | No dismissal or parent interaction. |
| Swipe down to dismiss compact sheet | Commit the draft before dismissal. This task has no unsaved draft after automatic dismissal; never interpret the gesture as Cancel. |
| Other automatic dismissal, including Escape if supported | Commit before closing; only explicit Cancel discards. |
| App interruption | Retain session state and preview for resumption; do not treat backgrounding as Cancel. If the session must close, commit first. |
| Width/orientation change | Transfer the session as described above; no exit semantics. |

At the root, show leading Cancel and trailing Done; these clarify rollback versus commit. In detail views show Back and Done, without a simultaneous Cancel. Returning to the root exposes Cancel again. Done works from either route. On dismissal restore editor selection and focus to Format unless a replacement control deliberately takes focus.

Compact parent content is unavailable for editing while the modal sheet is open. On wide layouts the palette must not hide essential preview context. Changes committed by Done or automatic dismissal form one undoable formatting operation per session (product decision). If persistence fails, retain the draft and show an explicit failure state with retry; never silently dismiss or claim it was saved.

## Guidance basis

These are local design decisions informed by the installed HIG snapshot, not verified SDK behavior. Anchoring, no cascades, retaining multi-selection, saving on automatic dismissal, and compact adaptation follow [Popovers — Best practices and iOS/iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers). Sheet sizing and action placement follow [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets). Saving on sheet swipe is a deliberate adaptation of the palette's automatic-save contract: there is no pending unsaved work to discard after that exit. [Layout — Adaptability and Size classes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) supports environment-based adaptation and state preservation. Platform context follows [Designing for iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ipados) and [Designing for iOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios).
EOF"

# Formatting palette repair

Patched interface.md in place, replacing the supplied defect summary with a concrete presentation, editing, and exit contract.

## Decisions and changes

- Wide layouts use a single content-sized popover anchored to the actual Format control. Secondary options stay within that surface, replacing the cascading popover.
- Compact layouts use an expanded modal sheet. Available space and size class determine adaptation, including narrow iPad windows; device identity alone does not.
- A stable selection, opening baseline, and working draft define the editing session. Multiple choices keep it open. Done and automatic dismissal commit; explicit Cancel alone rolls back.
- Rotation/resizing preserves the draft and route. Added focus restoration, save-failure retention, parent-interaction rules, and one undo operation per committed session.

The first three decisions follow [Popovers](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers#Best-practices). Sheet action placement and sizing draw on [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets#iOS-iPadOS); adaptive sizing draws on [Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout#Adaptability). Large-only initial sizing, draft/preview mechanics, undo grouping, and saving on sheet swipe are product decisions. The sheet guide calls for resolving unsaved work on swipe; this specification resolves it by committing, consistent with the transient palette's automatic-save policy. A future deferred-save task would need a separate dismissal-protection design.

## Worked before/after

Illustrative scenario: a person selects a heading, opens Format, selects Bold, then Italic, and opens secondary options.

Before, the brief says the first choice closes the palette, secondary options cascade, and outside tapping discards edits. On compact iPhone the same tiny floating geometry is used. The brief does not provide a rendered example or concrete formatting controls; Bold and Italic here are illustrative.

After, both choices remain in one draft while the palette stays open. Secondary options replace its body; Back retains the choices. On wide iPad, tapping outside commits both choices and closes the anchored popover. Explicit Cancel instead restores the opening formatting. If the window narrows mid-session, the same target, choices, and detail route move to the sheet. Done or swipe dismissal commits; no tiny popover remains on the phone.

## Acceptance checks and status

Static specification checks passed by reading the revised artifact:

| Check | Required contract now present |
|---|---|
| Anchor and context | Arrow targets the visible trigger; unavailable anchor falls back to sheet. |
| One presentation | No cascades; replacement closes and saves in one activation. |
| Repeated choices | Multiple choices retain the open palette and draft. |
| Data outcomes | Outside dismissal saves; Cancel discards only this session; Done commits. |
| Compact adaptation | Large sheet, safe-area controls, scrolling, no tiny floating geometry. |
| Continuity | Resize, rotation, interruption, and internal Back retain state. |

Runtime acceptance checks — all **not executed**:

1. On wide iPad, open Format near each window edge; verify arrow attachment and visible essential preview context. Resize through intermediate widths and rotate while on a detail route; verify one surface, unchanged target/draft, and preserved route.
2. Choose two independent formatting options; verify neither closes the palette. Exercise Done, Cancel, outside tap, replacement trigger, and supported Escape separately; reopen and inspect document formatting and undo history against the exit table.
3. On compact iPhone and narrow iPad, verify expanded sheet geometry, unavailable parent interaction, no outside-tap dismissal, and save-on-swipe. Verify Back only navigates, and Cancel remains available at the root.
4. Repeat in short landscape space and with enlarged text and long labels; verify scrolling reaches every action without overlap or shrunken controls. Exercise touch and supported keyboard/pointer paths.
5. Interrupt and resume; verify selection and draft survive. Inject a persistence failure and verify the draft remains available for retry. Verify actual focus restoration and assistive-technology navigation separately.

Failed checks: none established by static review. The original brief describes failures, but no executable UI was supplied to reproduce them. Static passes establish specification coverage only.

## Evidence and limits

Read the installed root apple-hig/SKILL.md explicitly, searched references/topic-index.md, then read the Getting started family and iOS/iPadOS topic procedures before their source guides; Presentation family and Popovers/Sheets procedures before their guides; and Foundations family and Layout procedure before its guide. No device, simulator, SDK compilation, GUI, physical reach, animation, native positioning, or accessibility execution was performed. Framework, OS availability, actual control inventory, and native dismissal implementation remain unspecified and require implementation validation.
EOF"

# Transient formatting palette — revised specification

Platforms: iPadOS and iOS. The palette edits formatting for the current document selection. It remains a short contextual task; it is not a persistent inspector. No framework or deployment version is specified.

## Presentation and layout

- A Format control opens the palette and captures the selected content as its editing target. Keep that target stable while using palette controls.
- In a regular-width environment with sufficient space, present one content-sized popover. Anchor its arrow directly to the visible Format control's bounds, updating the anchor as the window changes. Keep the control and essential selected-content reference visible; never point into empty space.
- Show primary formatting choices together. Reveal secondary formatting options inside the same surface with disclosure and an internal detail view. Back returns to the primary choices without saving, discarding, or closing. Never cascade a second popover. Animate content-size changes as one continuing surface.
- In compact width, use a modal sheet occupying the available width instead of tiny floating geometry. Start expanded at the large detent, with a scrollable body and fixed, reachable completion controls. Use standard centered sheet sizing on iPad when this fallback is needed. Do not offer a medium detent in this initial specification; therefore no resize grabber is needed.
- Select the surface from the current size class and usable space, not the device name. If a regular-width popover cannot fit its content while retaining the anchor and essential reference, use the sheet fallback. Keep controls inside safe areas; wrap/stack content rather than shrinking it. Short heights and enlarged text must retain access to every choice and completion action through scrolling.
- Resize or rotation transfers the active session between surfaces without a second presentation, commit, rollback, or reset. Preserve target, selected choices, draft, internal route, and scroll position where applicable. If the source control becomes unavailable, use the sheet rather than retain a detached arrow.

## Editing and exits

Maintain an opening baseline, a working formatting draft, and a stable target. Choices update a preview of that draft on the target; a preview is not yet a document commit. Each choice stays selected visibly. Both single and multiple choices leave the palette open so people can make a sequence of adjustments.

| Event | Required outcome |
|---|---|
| Done | Commit the draft to the target, dismiss, and return focus to Format. |
| Cancel | Explicitly discard this session's draft, restore the baseline preview, dismiss, and return focus to Format. Previously committed changes remain intact. |
| Tap outside wide popover | Commit the draft before dismissing. Never discard work. The dismissing tap must not also edit underlying document content. |
| Activate another contextual popover trigger | Commit and close the current popover, then open the replacement in the same activation. At most one popover is visible. |
| Back within detail options | Return within the same palette; retain all draft choices. |
| Tap outside compact modal sheet | No dismissal or parent interaction. |
| Swipe down to dismiss compact sheet | Commit the draft before dismissal. This task has no unsaved draft after automatic dismissal; never interpret the gesture as Cancel. |
| Other automatic dismissal, including Escape if supported | Commit before closing; only explicit Cancel discards. |
| App interruption | Retain session state and preview for resumption; do not treat backgrounding as Cancel. If the session must close, commit first. |
| Width/orientation change | Transfer the session as described above; no exit semantics. |

At the root, show leading Cancel and trailing Done; these clarify rollback versus commit. In detail views show Back and Done, without a simultaneous Cancel. Changes committed by Done or automatic dismissal form one undoable formatting operation per session (product decision). If persistence fails, retain the draft and show an explicit failure state with retry; never silently dismiss or claim it was saved.
